rows.annotation: tRNA pseudouridine(13) synthase TruD, converting uridine at position 13 of tRNA to pseudouridine.
rows.evidence: Query InterProScan identifies TruD through HAMAP, PANTHER, PFAM and its conserved catalytic site. Fitness Browser homologs at 77% identity are annotated TruD, and Dickeya homologs at 40.9–41.7% explicitly identify tRNA pseudouridine(13) synthase. The 99.7%-identity STRING homolog belongs to the TruD U13 orthogroup. Fitness phenotypes and the phenol-tolerance insertion do not establish a distinct molecular activity; no EC number or exclusive tRNA species specificity is assigned.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier A is supported by convergent query-specific TruD signatures, homolog locus annotations and the near-identical STRING homolog's orthogroup assignment. Literature summaries, fitness, neighborhood, STRING and topology evidence are present, but no supplied manuscript directly biochemically characterizes a close homolog and no cofitness data are provided. The distant xylose-receptor comparison is rejected because it conflicts with the extensive TruD domain evidence and predicted cytoplasmic topology; heterogeneous growth phenotypes do not justify assigning a metabolic substrate or phenol-detoxification function.

Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
